answer_text: A carbon atom has four electrons in its outer shell. Losing or gaining four electrons would give a C4+ or C4- ion, wich is energetically unfavourable, especially as the atom is small and holds its electrons tightly. Carbon therfore shares four electron pairs and is tetravalent. Becuase the C-C bond is strong, carbon atoms also join one another in long chains, branches and rings. This catenation, together with tetravalency, produces the huge variety of organic compounds.
